AgERA5 covariates in PlackettLuce models

ag5_plackett_luce.Rmd

Overview

PlackettLuce models the probability of ranking outcomes and is widely used for farmer-participatory variety trials using the tricot approach. pltree() extends this by partitioning trial sites into groups with distinct variety preferences, using environmental variables as splitting covariates.

This article demonstrates how to:

  1. Derive location and date information from a tricot trial dataset.
  2. Extract AgERA5 growing-season weather covariates with ag5_extract().
  3. Use those covariates in a pltree() model.

Packages 

library(ag5Tools)
library(PlackettLuce)

Trial data: beans

The beans dataset in PlackettLuce contains 842 tricot observations from a bean variety trial in Nicaragua (2015–2016). Each row records which of three randomly assigned varieties a farmer rated as best and worst.

library(PlackettLuce)
#> Warning: package 'PlackettLuce' was built under R version 4.5.3
data(beans)
str(beans[, c("variety_a", "variety_b", "variety_c",
              "best", "worst", "lon", "lat", "planting_date", "season")])
#> 'data.frame':    842 obs. of  9 variables:
#>  $ variety_a    : chr  "BRT 103-182" "INTA Rojo" "INTA Ferroso" "INTA Centro Sur" ...
#>  $ variety_b    : chr  "SJC 730-79" "INTA Centro Sur" "INTA Matagalpa" "INTA Rojo" ...
#>  $ variety_c    : chr  "PM2 Don Rey" "INTA Sequia" "BRT 103-182" "ALS 0532-6" ...
#>  $ best         : chr  "C" "B" "A" "B" ...
#>  $ worst        : chr  "A" "A" "C" "C" ...
#>  $ lon          : num  -85.7 -85.4 -85.4 -85.4 -85.4 ...
#>  $ lat          : num  13.1 13.3 13.3 13.3 13.3 ...
#>  $ planting_date: Date, format: "2015-12-18" "2015-12-18" ...
#>  $ season       : Factor w/ 5 levels "Po - 15","Ap - 15",..: 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 ...

The columns lon, lat, and planting_date give us everything needed to pull growing-season weather from AgERA5 for each observation.

Step 1: Derive a date range for each observation

Bean trials in this dataset run approximately 90 days. We add an end_date column from planting_date + 90.

beans$end_date <- beans$planting_date + 90
range(beans$planting_date)
#> [1] "2015-09-10" "2017-01-10"
range(beans$end_date)
#> [1] "2015-12-09" "2017-04-10"

Step 2: Extract AgERA5 covariates

We extract two growing-season covariates:

  • Total rainfall — sum of daily Precipitation-Flux (mm) over the growing season.
  • Mean maximum temperature — mean of daily Temperature-Air-2m (Max-24h, °C).

The ag5_extract() function accepts a data.frame as coords. We need to rename columns to match the expected default names (lon, lat, start_date, end_date), or pass the column names explicitly.

library(ag5Tools)

# Use explicit column names since beans uses 'planting_date' not 'start_date'
precip_list <- ag5_extract(
  coords     = beans,
  lon        = "lon",
  lat        = "lat",
  start_date = "planting_date",
  end_date   = "end_date",
  variable   = "Precipitation-Flux",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data"
)

maxt_list <- ag5_extract(
  coords     = beans,
  lon        = "lon",
  lat        = "lat",
  start_date = "planting_date",
  end_date   = "end_date",
  variable   = "Temperature-Air-2m",
  statistic  = "Max-24h",
  celsius    = TRUE,
  path       = "C:/agera5_data"
)

# Aggregate daily series to trial-level covariates
beans$total_rain <- sapply(precip_list, sum,  na.rm = TRUE)
beans$mean_maxt  <- sapply(maxt_list,  mean, na.rm = TRUE)

To download the AgERA5 files for Nicaragua before extracting:

# Nicaragua bounding box: c(north, west, south, east)
ag5_download(
  variable  = "precipitation_flux",
  year      = c(2015, 2016),
  month     = "all",
  day       = "all",
  area      = c(15, -88, 11, -83),
  path      = "C:/agera5_data"
)

ag5_download(
  variable  = "2m_temperature",
  statistic = "24_hour_maximum",
  year      = c(2015, 2016),
  month     = "all",
  day       = "all",
  area      = c(15, -88, 11, -83),
  path      = "C:/agera5_data"
)

Step 3: Convert rankings to PlackettLuce format

as.rankings() converts the tricot best/worst choices into a complete partial ranking matrix suitable for PlackettLuce() and pltree().

# Build a grouped_rankings object from the tricot best/worst format
R <- rank_tricot(data      = beans,
                 items     = c("variety_a", "variety_b", "variety_c"),
                 input     = c("best", "worst"),
                 group     = TRUE)

Step 4: Fit a PlackettLuce tree

pltree() uses the environmental covariates to partition the trial sites. Terminal nodes with meaningfully different worth estimates indicate that variety performance depends on growing conditions.

pl_tree <- pltree(R ~ total_rain + mean_maxt,
                  data    = beans,
                  minsize = 50)

print(pl_tree)
plot(pl_tree)

Step 5: Inspect worth estimates by node

itempar() returns the worth (log-ability) of each variety within each terminal node, revealing which varieties perform best under wetter or hotter conditions.

itempar(pl_tree)

Adding more covariates

The same workflow extends to any AgERA5 variable. Further covariates commonly used in variety trial analyses:

Covariate AgERA5 variable Statistic Aggregation
Growing-season solar radiation Solar-Radiation-Flux — sum ÷ 1e6 (MJ/m²)
Heat stress days Temperature-Air-2m Max-24h count days > 35 °C
Drought stress days Precipitation-Flux — count days < 1 mm
Mean vapour pressure Vapour-Pressure Mean mean (hPa) 
radn_list <- ag5_extract(
  coords     = beans,
  lon        = "lon",
  lat        = "lat",
  start_date = "planting_date",
  end_date   = "end_date",
  variable   = "Solar-Radiation-Flux",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data"
)

beans$total_radn <- sapply(radn_list, sum, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6  # MJ/m²

pl_tree2 <- pltree(R ~ total_rain + mean_maxt + total_radn,
                   data    = beans,
                   minsize = 50)
plot(pl_tree2)
